title: What You Gonna Do and Hungry Williams
summary: The B-side, its players, and how few drummers can play like Hungry Williams, who was ill and untraceable.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Okay. I was, there's another, there's a song I wanted to ask you. Is that what? It's the flip side of, of when I meet my girls. It's called What You Gonna Do.

Now, you know, see that too? I think that too could have been a record on the flip side of something else. See, because back then, they didn't turn records over too much. Mm-hmm. Like they do, you know, later on. And Larry McKinley would always say, man, this could have been a hit back. He's like that. What you gonna do?

And what it was, it was a little different from the regular shuffle kind of thing. And right now, I have difficulties playing unless it's rehearsed. That's why I never do. You got to rehearse that. You can't just play it, you know, like we play others. You got to rehearse this. That was Harold Batiste. That was that, that, um...

Charlie Williams on drums. Um, uh, what his name? What died? David Lashley. The trumpet player of Lashley's brother. Lee Allen. Or, uh, oh, it was in Red Tile, I know. That was just a good record. You know what? I'd sit down now and listen to that.
I think the difficulty may have come in with the drum and the...
Yeah, well, Hungry, yeah. Ain't nobody gonna play like Hungry.

And you know what? Even now, there's one white drummer. He's stout. He's got a beard. And he, he about, in his early fathers, because he's from the other school. And he would always say, man, I could play it. And sure enough, I played back, what, out on Western Boulevard. What that club is out there? Out there in the Western Boulevard, next door to the big restaurant. Um, well, anyway, I played... Huh?

No, not Barts. If you call the name, I don't know. But anyway, and when he was having this thing about five years ago, I played out there. I did this thing with this white band. And the drummer, and I told him about it. I said, man, that's Hungry. He said, I can play it. And sure enough, when I went to rehearsal, he played it. You know, very few drummers can play like Hungry. Because he was very unorthodox. He did everything on the other side. Just like Professor Long, you had to study it to play it. And he played it. And I said, man, look, that's the first time I ran into a drummer who can really play that stuff, you know. Because all the drummers that I ran into, even on When I Meet My Girl, they can't play that. Very rhythmic. I wish Hungry was around now. You know, I wondered, you know, they were looking for Hungry. They couldn't find him. The union had money for him. They couldn't find him.

Mm-hmm. He came down here, and he was sick. He went to Charity Hospital, and he came out of Charity Hospital, and he went on back to New York. Even his brother didn't know how to find him. So I'm going to ask Mr. Crump, too. Did they find Hungry? I'm going to ask him that tomorrow. Because they had some money. You know, from this, it's like a rug, it's from this theater thing that you get every so often. And it was about $400, $500. And I know Hungry could use it, because from what I can understand, he was in bad shape.
Yeah. Well, he was, he's like a guy, I guess, to be alive. He's a man, you know. He's, yeah, he's a man.
